LESSON: RESPONDING TO

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.2: Responding to

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Responding to
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What do you do when instructions and learner should be able to: answering questions in pairs or you want something?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. respond confidently to simple oral groups
2. use appropriate words in giving my family, my home, my school, and responding to instructions and my community) 129 questions

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Responding to

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Responding to

Teach
• Focus skill: respond confidently to simple oral groups.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Responding to.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Responding to
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do when instructions and learner should be able to: answering questions in pairs or you want something?
2. when asked to do 2 lessons different media instructions and questions(Myself, something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
